intended_object: The mixin class saying that addition `(x, y) ↦ x + y` on a pseudo-metric additive monoid is Lipschitz jointly in both arguments, i.e. there is a C with dist(x+y, x'+y') ≤ C·dist((x,y),(x',y')). This is inferred from the docstring, the module documentation, and its relation to `LipschitzMul`, whose additive version it is meant to be.
explanation:
The body is `∃ C, LipschitzWith C fun p : β × β => p.1 + p.1`. This only says that the doubling map x ↦ x + x is Lipschitz. It says nothing about addition of two different arguments. The multiplicative version right below it is written correctly as `p.1 * p.2`, and so are all the lemmas derived through `to_additive` (for example `lipschitz_with_lipschitz_const_add`, about `p.1 + p.2`). So the class does not match its own docstring or its multiplicative twin.

Concrete discrepancy: take any additive group of exponent 2, such as `ZMod 2` or (Set ℕ, symmetric difference). There `p.1 + p.1 = 0` is constant, so the class holds with C = 0 for every pseudo-metric. Now give such a group a pseudo-metric for which addition is discontinuous. Then addition is not jointly Lipschitz, yet the class still holds. Going the other way, if a metric makes x ↦ 2x Lipschitz, that does not make addition jointly Lipschitz. So the class defines a different property from the intended one.
